title: Commit save-share README and pending SPEAR world work
objective: Review the current dirty worktree, create proper local commit(s) for the uncommitted SPEAR world/import/docs work, and provide a GitHub URL other developers can use to follow the save/share process.
instructions: Inspect git status, diffs, remotes, branch tracking, and large/untracked files before staging.
Commit the root README save/share guidance and other meaningful uncommitted SPEAR world/import/docs/code changes that are appropriate for Git.
Do not blindly commit generated packet/session/log churn unless it is part of the intended repository state; explicitly report anything left uncommitted and why.

Check for GitHub-hosting constraints before including large Unreal binary assets. If files exceed normal GitHub limits and Git LFS is not configured, do not create an unusable commit; report the archive/artifact alternative.
Use clear commit message(s), preferably one commit if the staged scope is coherent, multiple only if necessary.

After committing, provide a GitHub URL to the README save/share section. If producing a working URL requires publishing, push only to origin, not upstream, preferably a new non-main branch if local main is diverged. Do not force-push, do not push to upstream, and do not open a PR.
If push/auth/divergence/size constraints prevent a valid GitHub URL, report the local commit SHA and the exact URL that will become valid after pushing to the user's fork.
constraints: Do not push to upstream or spear-sim/spear.
Do not discard or revert user changes.
expected_outputs: Commit SHA(s), commit message(s), and staged scope summary.
List of files intentionally left uncommitted, especially generated artifacts or large assets.
GitHub URL for other developers to read the save/share process, or a precise blocker if no pushed URL exists.
definition_of_done: Relevant changes are committed locally, or a precise blocker is reported before any unsafe commit.
No upstream push, no force push, no PR.
User receives a valid share URL if safely publishable, otherwise a precise next step.
